findings.title: The record's SOLE reader hard-codes one of the two `ratified_by` values the walk just admitted
findings.recommendation: Option A widened `not-ready` to `ratified_by: "ai" | "user"` — the AI's own dissent, or a human's. Step 5.65's readout example still says `archived against this session's own judgement`, and the requirement it implements says `the author's own judgement` (specs/orbit-archive-modifications/spec.md, THE READINESS LINE). When a USER ratified the not-ready, both lines attribute the dissent to the AI session that wrote the emit. This matters more than a wording slip because the readout is the record's ONLY reader — the second reader is explicitly deferred in design.md:36 — so the surface that keeps this record from being write-only misreports half the domain the walk just opened. It is also the exact pattern this cycle keeps naming: the fix landed on the instance (the validator) and stopped at the edge of the class (everything downstream of `ratified_by`). FIX: make the line read `ratified_by` — e.g. `readiness: NOT READY — archived against the author's own judgement (ai)` / `(user, ratified)` — and reword the requirement so it does not presuppose the AI authored the dissent.

findings.title: The archive's `SHALL carry a continuation entry` is unsatisfiable when no independent pass precedes the override
findings.recommendation: The new requirement paragraph says the archive emit SHALL carry a `continuation/proceed` entry whenever Step 3.4 is answered Proceed anyway. But `formed_against` must be NON-EMPTY and must cite INDEPENDENT passes that already exist on the trail, and `review-system` is unpassed precisely when the cadence is incomplete — including the case where it has no independent pass at all. In that case the SHALL cannot be satisfied: the author must either omit the record (leaving `gate_overridden` with no successor) or invent a token (refused). Measured rather than asserted: across all 10 archived changes, 20 emits carry `gate_overridden`, and for every one of them at least one independent pass token strictly precedes the emit — so 0/20 hit this edge and nothing is broken today. It still leaves rc04c's retirement premise incomplete, because `gate_overridden` covers a domain the successor provably cannot: the override's own trigger condition includes the state where the record is unwritable. FIX: settle the edge in the requirement — when no independent pass precedes the override, the entry is OMITTED and `gate_overridden` stands alone — and name it as a case rc04c must handle rather than a gap it will discover.

findings.title: `explore.md` — the DECLARED shared source for rc04b and rc04c — still states two things this change now refuses
findings.recommendation: D-rc04-15 (line 275) still specifies `not-ready` as `carrying the destination D-rc04-3 names (architecture) and being a RATIFIED disposition rather than an autonomous one` — the exact shape the walk retired, and which the engine now refuses (`destination` is an unknown key; `ratified_by: "ai"` is accepted). Line 281 still reads `THE ENGINE RULE, and it is the only one`, where three computed refusals shipped. explore.md's own header declares it the shared source cited by all three children, so rc04b and rc04c will read these as live. Worth noting the exploration was RIGHT and the proposal walk was wrong: D-rc04-16 (line 311) already separates the two cases — routing goes on the `address-reviews` emit, and `not-ready` at archive `is the honest dissent case`. The proposal-stage walk conflated them by bolting `destination` onto the archive case; option A restores D-rc04-16 rather than inventing anything. FIX: do NOT rewrite D-rc04-15 — explore.md's convention supersedes by APPENDING. Add a dated D-rc04-19 recording that the archive-carried `not-ready` sheds its destination and takes either `ratified_by` value, and that the ordering rule is the only computed rule ABOUT THE EVIDENCE.

findings.title: Task 3.1 still names the token source that this same walk proved cannot answer
findings.recommendation: F2 established by execution that `orbit status --change --json` carries no pass tokens and, post-move, does not resolve the change at all. The walk corrected all three workflow bodies — archive, apply and review now name the trail listing — and corrected task 2.5. Task 3.1 was missed: it still reads `which the body already reads from \`orbit status --change --json\`; \`formed_against\` is those passes' tokens`. A grep confirms it is the single surviving instance in the change's artifacts and the bodies, so this is residue of the walk itself rather than a missed site. It matters because tasks.md is the artifact a later reader consults to learn what the body was supposed to do, and it now teaches the disproved source. FIX: replace the clause with the trail listing the bodies name.

findings.title: F6's third cited site is neither fixed nor routed — the stage declaration still says THE ONE COMPUTED RULE
findings.recommendation: F6 cited three sites asserting a single computed constraint: proposal.md:44, design.md's D3, and the stage declaration. The walk amended the first two — F6's own FIX text asked for exactly those — and `orbit architecture show clean-up-review-cycle rc04a-judgement-record` confirms the third still reads `THE ONE COMPUTED RULE: every token in formed_against MUST precede...`. A stage change correctly does not edit program-layer docs, which is why task 6.4 exists and already routes two other residues plus the exit-(3) revision. This one is simply absent from that list, so it is a finding resolved on the instances and dropped at the edge of its own class. FIX: add it to 6.4's architect list — the stage declaration's ONE COMPUTED RULE line should name the ordering rule as the one rule about the record's relation to its EVIDENCE, with the carrier-kind and gate-agreement refusals named as shape/location constraints, the second retiring with `gate_overridden` in rc04c.

findings.title: `judgements` was added to a schema block no parity instrument reads
findings.recommendation: The parity test covers four references (review / address-reviews / audit-drift / archive `run-summary-schema.md` + `archive-summary-schema.md`). The `review-external` T0 record's schema block lives in `orbit-review/references/external-handoff.md`, which is not in the REFERENCES table — so of the three CARRIERS this change ships, one has its documented shape checked against the payload table, one (`apply`) has no schema reference at all, and one (`review-external`) has a reference the instrument does not read. Verified there is no actual divergence today: the block's `judgements` key is accepted by `payloadFieldsFor('review-external')`. This is the same instrument argument the fresh half made for the missing archive field-note, which is why it is worth recording rather than assuming. Pre-existing rather than caused here — but rc04a is what added a field to the unread block. FIX (or route): add `review-external` to the parity REFERENCES table with `external-handoff.md`, declaring `reviewer_class`/`awaiting_findings` engine-owned; if that is past this stage's ceiling, name it in task 6.4 instead of leaving it undiscovered.

findings.title: The prototype-kind regression test does not assert the thing the finding was about
findings.recommendation: F3's complaint was not that `kind: "toString"` failed to refuse — exit code and no-write already held — but that the refusal `names an internal identifier instead` of the offending value, against task 2.5's stated contract that every refusal names it. The regression case added in the walk asserts `/'kind' must be one of/`, which is the message PREFIX and would still pass if the message omitted the value entirely. The test therefore covers the crash and not the contract the finding was raised under. FIX: tighten the pattern to require the value — `/'kind' must be one of .* got "toString"/` — so the assertion matches the defect.

stale_suppressed.title: The second reader D-rc04-16 promised (`orbit status --change` surfacing the latest readiness record) is not built
stale_suppressed.evidence: Verified before raising and SUPPRESSED as not-a-finding: design.md:36-37 defers it explicitly with a reason ('exit (4) is satisfied by the first reader, and adding orbit-orientation would put this change past the ceiling'), and design.md:139-140 records it again under accepted tradeoffs. Confirmed by grep that `judgements` appears nowhere in orientation.ts, report-render.ts or artifact-graph/ — i.e. the absence is the declared scope, not an omission. A deferral that is stated twice with its R-crc-1 reason is a scope decision, not a defect.

commentary:
This is the trailing in-context slot, run immediately after a 14-finding blind-pair walk, and the result is what that position is for rather than a second opinion on the same tree: FOUR of the five warnings are residue of the walk itself, none of them visible to either independent half, because neither half could see what the walk would do.

The pattern is one shape in four places. A fix lands where the reviewer pointed and stops at the edge of the class it belonged to. The validator learned that `not-ready` takes either `ratified_by` value; the readout that is its only consumer did not. Three workflow bodies learned where pass tokens actually live; the task that specified them did not. Proposal and design learned there is more than one computed rule; the stage declaration — a site the finding itself cited — was neither fixed nor routed. That is the same diagnosis this cycle has now produced at four consecutive stages, and it is worth saying plainly that the walk which named the pattern in its own commit message then committed it four times in one sitting. The class is not hard to see in hindsight; it is hard to see while fixing.

One finding is not residue and is the most interesting thing here. The archive's continuation requirement is an unsatisfiable SHALL at the edge of its own domain — the override fires when the cadence is incomplete, which includes having no independent pass to cite, and the successor record requires a non-empty citation. I resisted asserting it and measured instead: 20 recorded `gate_overridden` emits across 10 archived changes, and for every one at least one independent pass token strictly precedes it. So 0/20, nothing broken, and the severity reflects that. But the domain hole is real and it is rc04c's premise that pays for it, which is the kind of thing worth writing down while it is cheap rather than discovering inside the stage that depends on it.

What I probed hardest and found clean: delta fidelity, scenario by scenario against the live baselines, since I had edited two MODIFIED blocks and this repo's characteristic defect is exactly that — zero dropped, zero body-changed, eleven added. The refusal ordering (unknown-key before kind), which makes the carrier map's `admitted &&` guard unreachable for unlisted commands rather than lax. And one candidate I verified and suppressed rather than report: the missing second reader is a twice-stated deferral with its ceiling reason, not an omission.

What I cannot assess from this seat, and will not pretend otherwise: whether the engine changes this walk made are themselves correct. I wrote them. The two defects the external half found were both rules that read correctly and computed wrongly, and an in-context pass reading its own code is the worst-positioned reader for that failure mode. Everything above is a consistency argument or a measurement; none of it is independent verification of the validator.
